items.title: Cosimo Matassa Interview, 1994-01-15
items.q: We were, we were, we were always good friends and all that

ctx.x: Was Jerry Wexler involved with this suit?

Well, Wexler and, and, and, and Ahmet were, were, you know, it was kind of strange, you know. We were, we were, we were always good friends and all that, but we had this battle going on. We'd get on the phone and they'd tell me, you know, this thing is ours. You know, and I said, no, no, it's mine. You know, I mean, we, we, we were talking about it on the phone, you know. And saying, hey, they're not, not as lawyer to lawyer, but as person to person. And, and, and, and, and they said, well, you know, we're going…
So you were students in, in federal court or?

items.title: Cosimo Matassa Interview, 1993-11-01
items.q: Interviewer mentions Jerry Wexler in the context of publishing rights and Alan Freed; Interviewee responds about the song existing before Wexler recorded it, but does not describe a personal or professional relationship with Wexler himself.

ctx.x: Well, it didn't surprise me when this person told me.

Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. So it was a woman? It was a woman. Jerry Hall. Oh, Jerry. Oh, yeah. Yeah, it was Jerry. Yeah. Jerry's crazy. Crazy woman. Yeah. But, you know, there were things like that. Like I say, I remember Blackwell. And Earl Palmer.

items.title: Cosimo Matassa Interview, 1993-07-17
items.q: So, you didn't have to tell Ahmed Erdogan, for instance, or Jerry Wexler what to do... But, but they were, they were a great team... Like at the end of the session... I appreciated that in them.

ctx.x: John, Jerry Wexler, or Lou Chud, something like that?

No, no, no. They were, they were, they were more, well, Chud was a, was an eternal cynic. But, but Wexler was, you know, New York, Jew turned atheist. And, and hard, sharp, experienced, you know, all of the things Jerry Wexler is.
